controller_actions.task: Rewrite module.py so that it exposes solve(data), using only the Python standard library and no I/O or dynamic code execution. Input is a list of POSIX-style path strings. Return normalized paths in input order, and do not mutate the input. Rules: an empty string raises ValueError. A path starting with '/' is absolute; otherwise it is relative. Collapse repeated slashes, drop '.' segments, and resolve each '..' against the preceding segment. For absolute paths, a '..' that would go above root raises ValueError. For relative paths, unresolvable leading '..' segments are kept. Drop a trailing slash, except the normalized root stays '/'. A relative path that normalizes to nothing becomes '.'. The current module.py is incorrect (it only replaces '//' once and does not resolve '.' or '..'); replace it entirely. Only write module.py.

Write test_cases.json only. It must be a JSON list of at least four distinct cases. Each case has an input field (a list of path strings) and exactly one of output (expected JSON result list) or error (exception class name, e.g. "ValueError"). Extra fields such as name are allowed. Expectations must follow this contract: collapse repeated slashes, drop '.' segments, resolve '..' against the preceding segment; for absolute paths, a '..' that would go above root raises ValueError; for relative paths, unresolvable leading '..' segments are kept; drop a trailing slash except the root stays '/'; a relative path that normalizes to nothing becomes '.'; an empty string raises ValueError; output is in input order. Use these verified cases: ["a/b"] -> ["a/b"]; ["/a//b/"] -> ["/a/b"]; ["/a/./b/../c"] -> ["/a/c"]; ["../../x/.."] -> ["../.."]; ["/.."] -> error ValueError; [""] -> error ValueError; ["/"] -> ["/"]; ["."] -> ["."]. Derive every expected value by applying the contract, not by copying module.py output. Write only test_cases.json and do not write module.py or any other file.
